ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening against FINTRAC's Politically Exposed Persons categories, Global Affairs Canada's sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act, Public Safety Canada and UN Security Council consolidated lists, and the U.S. OFAC SDN List where USD payment rails or Apple/Google payment processors require OFAC compliance. Enhanced due diligence is required for medium-risk interactive voice-streaming social apps, including positive identification of all 25%+ beneficial owners, source-of-funds verification for nomineeing or trust-controlled investors, and ongoing transaction monitoring for FINTRAC reporting obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (accessible through authorized service providers registered in Alberta, including ISC; online point of entry at alberta.ca/corporate-registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Alberta statutory corporate and limited partnership names must be expressed in English or French, using Roman alphabet letters and Arabic numerals. Names in non-Roman scripts or languages require a transliteration and an English/French translation. The name must follow the distinctive-element-descriptive-element-legal-element structure, and the legal element for an Alberta limited partnership must include 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' or words giving equivalent notice of limited liability.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant must file a written administrative review request with the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the rejection, supplying the NUANS name search report, a memorandum distinguishing the name from conflicting marks, and any consents from relevant professional governing bodies for sensitive tokens. If the administrative review is denied, the applicant may apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review within 60 days of the denial using the Alberta Rules of Court expedited procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for this unregulated voice-streaming social app business, provided a physical street address in Alberta is designated as the registered office and service address and is staffed or capable of receiving legal process during normal business hours. A post-office box alone is not acceptable. Cloud-hosted or non-Alberta infrastructure does not defeat commercial substance for Alberta limited partnership registration purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; less than 5% baseline annual probability for an unlicensed digital app business. Inspection risk rises materially if FINTRAC initiates an AML/CFT compliance examination, if service by registered mail fails, or if the Corporate Registry receives a complaint regarding non-receipt of documents at the registered office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, Part 2 (Limited Partnerships), ss 51-75; limited partnership registration is not effected under the Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Registration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1) filed under section 53 of the Partnership Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement under Alberta law; capital contributions are established by contract in the Limited Partnership Agreement
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, as resolutions of the board of directors of [General Partner], that: 1. The General Partner approves formation of the Alberta limited partnership and authorizes submission of the completed Registration of Limited Partnership to the Alberta Corporate Registry under the Partnership Act. 2. The registered office of the limited partnership shall be at [registered address], Alberta, and the registered office consent is approved. 3. [General Partner] is appointed as general partner, and [Name] is appointed as manager/officer with authority to open bank accounts and execute voice streaming platform, payment, and commercial contracts. 4. The Limited Partnership Agreement presented to this board is adopted and the General Partner is authorized to execute it on behalf of the limited partnership. 5. All actions taken by the incorporators and agents prior to this meeting are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry online portal, Service Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search through Service Alberta's online reservation service or a licensed service provider. Submit a name reservation request for the proposed limited partnership name; the name must not be confusingly similar to an existing registered name and must satisfy Alberta naming rules for limited partnerships. No notarization is required.
required_dossiers: Consent to use a name if the requested name is subject to a prior claim
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, request reconsideration from the Corporate Registry, submit alternate name preferences, and reserve a compliant name before continuing the registration filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Limited Partnership Agreement and Registration Statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal counsel and organizers; no government filing at this stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement setting out capital contributions, profit and loss allocation, management authority, and dissolution terms. Complete the Registration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1), identifying general partners, the registered office, and the contribution amount or agreed contribution obligations. Retain original signed documents.
required_dossiers: Registration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1) draft
Consent to act of each general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If internal documents are defective, amend and re-execute the agreement and form before any submission to the Registry; no public curing mechanism is needed until filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Registration with Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form LP-1 through the online Corporate Registry system or by courier to the Registrar of Companies. Pay the prescribed registration fee online by credit card or pre-authorized account. Upon approval, the Registry issues a Certificate of Registration evidencing the limited partnership's existence.
required_dossiers: Executed Registration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency notice, respond within the stated cure period, correct the form or resubmit the filing, and pay any applicable re-filing fee; administrative review may be requested if the filing is rejected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner's governing body and, if required, Alberta Corporate Registry for follow-up filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board resolution of the General Partner. Confirm the Alberta registered office, approve the registered office consent, ratify the appointment of the General Partner, and appoint a manager/officer with authority to open payment and platform accounts. Establish the partnership minute book and issue partnership interest records.
required_dossiers: Consent to act of officers or manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a governance step is omitted, ratify the action by written resolution of the General Partner and, where public records are affected, file the appropriate statement of change with the Corporate Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; Alberta Corporate Registry for annual maintenance; Alberta municipal authorities if a physical office is opened
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the Canada Revenue Agency for a Business Number (BN), including GST/HST registration if the partnership has taxable supplies in Canada. Maintain the Alberta registered office and file the annual return with the Corporate Registry. No separate municipal business licence is required for a purely virtual voice streaming platform unless physical premises are established.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA rejects or queries the registration, correct the BN application, provide supporting partnership documents, and call the CRA business enquiries line; if the annual return is flagged, file an amended return with the Corporate Registry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable; no industrial or manufacturing establishment is involved. Any future physical office is governed by the local municipality and Alberta Municipal Affairs.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required under Alberta or Canadian federal law for a voice streaming social application; standard privacy, consumer protection, and platform rules apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no environmental impact assessment registration or EIA screening is required for a non-physical digital-services platform.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater, VOC, or hazardous emissions are generated. If a physical office is later occupied, comply with municipal wastewater/sanitary bylaws and Alberta waste handling requirements for electronic waste and general refuse.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for a virtual operation. If physical premises are leased, obtain an occupancy certificate, pass fire safety inspection under the Alberta Fire Code, and comply with the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code before occupation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) - federal tax administration for GST/HST, income tax and T5013 partnership information returns. Digital portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-businesses/business-account.html) and Business Registration Online (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/registering-your-business/business-registration-online.html). Provincial counterpart for entity formation: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta / CORES) under the Partnership Act (RSA 2000, c. P-3). Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administers import/export program accounts (RM) where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Register the Alberta Limited Partnership under the Partnership Act (RSA 2000, c. P-3) through the Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta or authorized service provider) to obtain the provincial registration file number; no minimum capital is required and non-resident partners are permitted. Step 2 - Obtain the federal 9-digit Business Number (BN) for the partnership from CRA using Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1; the BN is the master identifier for all CRA program accounts. Step 3 - Register the LP itself as the GST/HST registrant under program account 'RT' (GST/HST); under ETA s. 123(1) a partnership is a 'person' for GST/HST purposes, so the partnership, not the individual partners, holds the registration and collects tax. Step 4 - Add other program accounts only if needed: 'RC' (corporate income tax - inapplicable to a flow-through LP unless it elects opaque treatment), 'RP' (payroll for any Canadian employees), 'RM' (import/export - not applicable to pure digital service exports). Step 5 - For foreign partners or foreign parent entities: CRA's non-resident registration desk accepts applications without a Canadian bank account; foreign identification documents and a completed representative authorization (or power of attorney) are required; the simplified non-resident digital-services GST/HST registration applies to foreign sellers making specified supplies to Canadian recipients. Step 6 - File the T5013 Partnership Information Return annually under the partnership BN and issue T5013 slips to all partners. Typical timelines: provincial registration 1-3 business days; CRA BN and GST/HST registration immediate when filed online or 2-4 weeks by paper.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - For Canadian income tax purposes the Alberta LP is fiscally transparent: no entity-level Part I tax is imposed; each partner's allocable share of income/loss is computed under ITA s. 96 and taxed in the hands of the partner. For GST/HST purposes the partnership is a separate 'person' (ETA s. 123(1)) and must register, collect and remit GST in its own name. Territorial scope: the LP carries on business in Canada through its Alberta establishment, making it a Canadian-resident partnership subject to Canadian tax on worldwide income as allocated to resident partners and on Canadian-source income allocated to non-resident partners; GST applies to supplies made in Canada based on place-of-supply rules. Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax (only 5% federal GST) and no provincial capital tax or general payroll tax. Tax_Exempt_Zone: not applicable - Canada and Alberta maintain no free-zone or special economic zone exemption for digital services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box regime; entity classification is statutory. Available elections directly relevant to an Alberta LP: (i) Canada-U.S. Tax Treaty Article IV(7) fiscal-transparency election - a U.S. entity (LLC or LP) that is fiscally transparent for U.S. tax may be recognized as fiscally transparent in Canada for treaty benefit purposes (CRA administrative position); (ii) ETA s. 273 joint election between a partnership and a registrant partner to treat supplies of taxable services as made for nil consideration; (iii) ETA s. 156 election for closely related corporations (inapplicable to a pure partnership but available if corporate subsidiaries are inserted); (iv) GST quick method (ETA s. 227) and annual filing elections for eligible small registrants; (v) ITA partnership elections regarding fiscal period and computation of income under s. 96; (vi) hybrid-mismatch rules under OECD BEPS Action 2 have been announced by the Department of Finance but are not yet enacted - no election currently exists to override a foreign opaque/transparent mismatch, and the LP should monitor draft legislation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) - federal value-added tax under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act. Alberta is a non-participating province with no provincial sales tax and no HST, so only the 5% federal GST applies to taxable supplies made in Alberta. A separate federal Digital Services Tax (3% under the Digital Services Tax Act, S.C. 2024, c. 15) applies only to groups with global digital services revenue above EUR 750 million and Canadian digital services revenue above CAD 20 million - expected to be below thresholds for this LP but must be monitored.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies in a 12-month period (the small-supplier threshold under ETA s. 148(1)). For the non-resident digital-services regime effective July 1, 2021, the same CAD 30,000 threshold applies to specified digital supplies made to Canadian recipients, determined under the 'Canadian recipient' rules (at least two of: Canadian IP address, Canadian billing address, Canadian bank account information, or Canadian telephone number). For a Canadian-resident Alberta LP, once combined taxable worldwide supplies including Apple IAP and Google Play Billing revenue exceed CAD 30,000, GST registration is mandatory from the earlier of the first day of the following month or quarter; voluntary registration is available below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no real-time fiscal clearance, API tax-clearance obligation or digital stamping mandate. Electronic filing of GST/HST returns is mandatory for registrants whose annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 1.5 million; registrants below this threshold may file electronically through GST/HST NETFILE. Since 2024, the voluntary Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Service operates over the Peppol network (OpenPeppol PINT specifications) but is not linked to tax clearance or pre-clearance validation. Invoices must display the Business Number and GST registration number; simplified invoices are permitted for supplies under CAD 150. All records, including invoices, Apple/Google payment settlement reports, server logs and IP-geolocation data, must be retained for six years and, if stored outside Canada, must be accessible electronically to CRA upon demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for exported digital services and intangible property is available under ETA Schedule VI. Part V, s. 7 zero-rates a supply of a service made to a non-resident person unless the service is in respect of real property situated in Canada, is in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed, or is rendered to an individual present in Canada at the time the service is rendered. Part IV zero-rates supplies of intangible personal property (including digital content and licences) made to non-resident persons. For the voice-streaming app: (i) subscriptions, virtual gifts and in-app consumables sold to end consumers resident outside Canada are zero-rated when billing address, payment method country code and IP geolocation are all non-Canadian; (ii) B2B advertising, licensing and API services supplied to non-resident platforms and ad networks are zero-rated under the same s. 7 test; (iii) supplies to Canadian consumers are taxable at 5% GST regardless of the seller's location; (iv) where Apple or Google acts as app-store platform operator, the platform-operator deemed-supplier rule applies only to non-resident, non-registered sellers - a Canadian-resident LP registrant is the principal supplier and must collect and remit GST on Canadian consumer transactions; (v) no zero-rating is available where the service is consumed in Canada or enjoyed by an individual present in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A / ACI eManifest) - not applicable to pure digital service exports; required only if physical goods (e.g., branded merchandise) are shipped from Canada and should not be relied upon for zero-rating substantiation

Bill of Lading - not applicable to service exports; substituted by execution and delivery logs evidencing service provision from Canadian servers to non-resident customers (account UID, IP-geolocation metadata, device fingerprint, session timestamps)

Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or Apple/Google payout settlement statements evidencing receipt of subscription and in-app purchase revenue from non-resident end users and B2B counterparties

Non-resident status substantiation: for B2B customers, an executed declaration of non-residency and GST/HST registration status (CRA attestation substantively equivalent to GST189 or U.S. W-8BEN-E); for B2C customers, billing address, payment method country code and IP-geolocation data captured at checkout
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA conducts data-driven audits of digital-platform settlement data, cross-matching Apple/Google payout records against declared Canadian versus foreign revenue and IP-geolocation analytics; zero-rating is denied where Canadian presence indicators (IP, SIM, billing address, payment method) are not rebutted by documentary evidence. Consequences of a failed zero-rating claim: (i) reassessment for uncollected 5% GST plus compound daily interest at the CRA prescribed rate (basic rate plus 4 percentage points; approximately 9% for arrears in late 2024) from the date remittance was due; (ii) the normal reassessment window is 4 years, but is unlimited where a misrepresentation is attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful default or fraud; (iii) penalties: failure to register - the greater of CAD 250 and 1% of collectible GST; failure to file - the greater of CAD 250 and 1% of net tax; false statements or omissions made knowingly or with gross negligence - the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the deficiency; (iv) partner liability: each general partner of the LP is jointly and severally liable for the partnership's GST obligations under ETA s. 272.1, while limited partners' liability is generally capped at contributed capital and undistributed returns; (v) deliberate evasion may attract criminal prosecution under ETA s. 327 with fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and/or imprisonment. Canada imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark is a documentary-control standard - unrepatriated revenue does not per se invalidate zero-rating, but prolonged non-repatriation weakens the evidentiary chain supporting the foreign-supply characterization and may invite economic-substance scrutiny.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a floating exchange rate regime with full convertibility for both current and capital accounts. Profit remittances to foreign partners or owners are permitted without prior approval, subject only to standard tax filing and beneficial ownership verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion requirement applies to export receipts. Digital service revenues, including in-app monetization from voice streaming, may be converted freely on the spot market through authorized dealers. Proceeds must be reported to Canada Revenue Agency for tax purposes within statutory timelines.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility rating for digital EMIs via partnerships with Apple App Store and Google Play Billing. Legal constraints include compliance with the federal Payment Act, PCI DSS requirements, and potential Alberta Money Services Business licensing for cross-border digital payment processing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted for Alberta Limited Partnerships through online portals with video KYC verification. In-person appearance by directors or authorized signers may be required for high-volume fintech accounts or complex ownership structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of funds or high-velocity international inflows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate charter, beneficial ownership certificate, source of wealth affidavit, and detailed transaction narrative

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent KYC documentation or suspicious activity indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan, revenue projections, and legal entity verification documents

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection'. Verification requires corporate resolution, proof of ownership, and full AML screening. Use of major correspondent banks for efficiency.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements via SWIFT MT103 for trade payments or Commercial Letters of Credit where applicable. Purpose codes must align with legitimate business expenses such as vendor payments or developer royalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the anniversary of the LP's registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee CAD 50; failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Registrar to administratively strike off the LP registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the anniversary of the LP's registration date; also upon any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offences subject to fines up to CAD 50,000 for the LP and CAD 10,000 per partner/general partner; persistent non-compliance may trigger registry strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatory under the Alberta Partnership Act. An independent audit may be required by the partnership agreement, lender covenants, or if the LP becomes a reporting issuer under Canadian securities laws. The LP is also not subject to a statutory audit merely by size or revenue.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) applies for private limited partnerships; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) is required if the LP is a publicly accountable enterprise or elects IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each transfer of a limited partnership interest must be recorded in the LP's internal register of limited partners. All changes in individuals with significant control must be reported to the Alberta Beneficial Ownership Registry and confirmed annually in the Beneficial Ownership Return, filed within 60 days of the LP registration anniversary.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book and Records of Resolutions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined federal and Alberta general corporate rate (15.0% federal + 8.0% Alberta); the Alberta LP is fiscally transparent, so this rate applies when a corporate partner is taxed on its share of LP income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction: combined 11.0% (9.0% federal + 2.0% Alberta) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income for a qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation partner; SR&ED refundable investment tax credits up to 35% of qualified expenditures; Alberta Innovation Employment Grant and other provincial credits available for digital media R&D

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013SUM Summary — filed electronically via CRA-approved XML/EFILE software or CRA Web Forms
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than five (5) months after the LP's fiscal period end; for a December 31 year end, the due date is May 31 of the following calendar year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered business address and CRA Business Number (BN) of the limited partnership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the LP's exact legal name registered with the Alberta Corporate Registry; obtain the BN through CRA Business Registration Online before filing

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period end date, which cannot exceed 12 months
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A December 31 year end is recommended; non-resident partners must report their share of LP income in their respective taxation years that include the LP's fiscal period end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indication of whether the partnership has any specified non-resident partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Answer Yes where any partner is not resident in Canada for treaty purposes; attach a supporting schedule identifying each non-resident partner's residence country, percentage share, and allocated income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Canadian active business income or loss for the fiscal period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the portion of active business income earned in Canada; non-resident partners carrying on business in Canada through the LP are taxable under Part I of the Income Tax Act on this share, subject to treaty relief

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Canadian investment income, including specified investment flow-through income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose separately any interest, dividends, and rental royalties; certain passive income of non-resident partners may attract Part XIII withholding or additional Part I allocations

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under ITA s.162(7): CAD 25 per day per partner, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500; gross negligence penalties up to CAD 100 per day (maximum CAD 2,500) plus 10% of unreported amounts; CRA prescribed interest compounded daily on any resulting partner-level tax balance

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporate Income Tax Return — filed by the corporate general partner or any corporate partner that carries on business through the LP
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 must be filed within six (6) months after the corporate partner's taxation year end; balance-due day is three (3) months after year end for a Canadian-controlled private corporation claiming the small business deduction and two (2) months for all other corporations

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate partner's legal name, BN, registered office, and Canadian or foreign jurisdiction of incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner carrying on business in Canada through the LP must file a T2, elect a Canadian agent, and disclose any permanent establishment in Alberta

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income, including the corporate partner's pro rata share of the LP's income or loss under ITA s.96
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate partnership income in accordance with the partnership agreement, ensuring allocations have substantive economic effect and are not designed solely to shift income to non-residents

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax at 15.0% general rate, or 9.0% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income eligible for the small business deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The small business deduction is denied where the corporate partner is non-resident or where the partnership income is 'specified partnership income' allocated to a partner holding 10% or more of the partnership interests

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta provincial tax at 8.0% general rate, or 2.0% on small-business-eligible income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Alberta tax applies if the corporate partner has a permanent establishment in Alberta through the LP's actual business operations, employees, or fixed place of business in the province

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delay up to 12 months; repeated failure penalty of 10% plus 2% per month up to 24 months; a non-resident corporate partner that fails to file may be assessed under ITA s.162 and may lose treaty access for the taxation year

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25.0% federal Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder; LP profit distributions to partners are not dividends and are not subject to dividend withholding, but each partner's share is taxed as ordinary income in the partner's hands and, for non-resident partners, is collected through Part I or Part XIII mechanisms as applicable
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident partner or shareholder seeking a reduced treaty rate must complete CRA Form NR301 (declaration for treaty benefits by an individual or entity) or Form NR302 (declaration for a partnership with non-resident members) and deliver it to the Canadian payer before payment; the recipient must obtain a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from its home jurisdiction tax authority and produce it to the CRA upon written demand; the payer and the LP must retain all forms in the corporate records; treaty relief is denied where the income is attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment of the non-resident
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25.0% statutory Part XIII withholding on payments for the use of software, copyrights, and other intangible property; the Canada-US treaty reduces most royalty payments to 10.0%; interest: 25.0% statutory Part XIII rate, but arm's-length interest paid to non-resident creditors is exempt under the domestic interest exemption (ITA s.212(1)(b)(vii)); non-arm's-length interest paid to related non-residents is subject to the 25.0% statutory rate and may be treaty-reduced (for example, 15.0% under Article XI of the Canada-US treaty)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory minimum threshold for Local File or Master File; contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is expected by the CRA where intercompany transactions exceed CAD 1,000,000 in aggregate for a taxation year, and the Country-by-Country (CbC) Report is mandatory where the multinational group's consolidated revenue is at least CAD 750,000,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Alberta has no UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, the CRA applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (ITA s.245), the doctrine of substance over form, and treaty anti-abuse rules (including Limitation-on-Benefits clauses) to disregard artificial arrangements; the LP must demonstrate real commercial substance in Alberta, including actual staff, physical or cloud infrastructure contracts, user-facing operational decision-making, and a valid commercial purpose for intercompany platform and IP arrangements

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting in-app subscription and virtual gifting revenue from the LP's T5013, or inflating deductible management, royalty, or platform fees paid to a related offshore entity to strip Canadian-source profit out of the tax net
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: On indictment, a fine of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded plus imprisonment for up to five (5) years under ITA s.239; on summary conviction, a fine of 50% to 200% of the evaded amount and imprisonment of up to two (2) years less a day; civil gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax under ITA s.163(2); CRA prescribed interest compounded daily on all reassessed amounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers and directors who direct, assent to, or participate in the filing of false returns are personally liable for civil penalties, may be prosecuted for fraud and tax evasion, and face criminal travel bans, asset freezes, and extradition from treaty partners
